rv.q: "1776" is a tricky piece in that the stakes could not be higher but the mood often is light.

But even if the show that opened Wednesday at the venerable north suburban theater existed beyond the unavoidable context of this year’s deeply contentious presidential race, it would still be a must-see musical.
The Marriott Theatre’s take on the founding of our nation hits on every level.
History comes alive in this intelligent and accessible musical, now in an incredibly captivating production at the Marriott Theatre.
So you can take my word that, from the first roll of a snare drum to the Liberty Bell sounding the final signature on the Declaration, the Marriott Theatre absolutely nails it.

What Lin-Manuel Miranda did for the U.S. Constitution, director extraordinaire Nick Bowling does for the Declaration of Independence in Marriott Theatre’s exquisitely modern-ish turn on the old-school-ish 1776.
Marriott Theatre’s “1776” has a sweeping professional sheen as one of the finest and most unique shows on stage right now.

One can't say the same about the less-than-memorable score. However, it's improved by a vocally impressive ensemble led by the formidable Tyrick Wiltez Jones, an exceptional singer whose impassioned performance as the independence-minded firebrand John Adams anchors this abridged history lesson.
This is probably the slickest version of "1776" ever!
Marriott Theatre's "1776" should definitely be on that "don't miss" list.
The seminal event in American history blazes to vivid life in this funny, insightful, and compelling drama.

cn.t: Critics praise this timely, brilliantly cast revival for its modern inclusivity and savvy direction, with most highlighting a magnificent second act that brings American history to life with unexpected humor and dramatic tension.
